analysis:
Examined both supplied test excerpts and the bounded patch. The patch at DistributedAutomaticBatchPlannerTests.swift:772–785 (head) changes the expected coordinator discovery behavior: auto may request the speculative assistant when this build declares it public for the artifact; explicit on remains supported. This is test evidence, not proof of production routing authorization or qualification. The base tests at :935–969 explicitly distinguish ordinary target qualification from assistant plans not offered for public traffic; :972–1078 exercise bilateral policy persistence, handoff compatibility, strict decoding and worker feature admission. The head excerpt at :128–389 exercises quote envelopes, retained geometry, memory admission, incumbent-weight credit, post-release refusal bookkeeping and rejection of foreign/stale/public measurement files. No concrete security regression is established by these test-only excerpts; no live prompt, key, cache, billing or attestation implementation is shown changing.
Integration must inspect the production declaration/discovery changes and reconcile them with public-serving configuration validation and final request admission (A-016/A-017, TB-011, T-052/T-054/T-056). A local public-artifact declaration must not substitute for coordinator authorization or independent build qualification. Also verify that assistant execution preserves request/cache scope (A-001, T-041), bilateral inventory binding and resource admission (A-018, TB-007). The head tests newly added at :791–834 and most modified assertions around :772–789 are outside the supplied head excerpt; the patch is truncated. These omissions and absent production source leave the new public-assistant contract unresolved, rather than demonstrating a missing control.
